prepared using high purity elements (0.999 Al, Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, Nb, and Ti, by weight) by Edmund Bühler MAM-1 vacuum arc melter with Turbomolecular pumping system HVT52/G under an Ar atmosphere. The alloy ingots with am a s so f3– 5 g were cast three times to ensure chemical homogeneity.
The alloys were then cast into 4 mm diameter copper moulds via suction casting for tension tests.

SEM micrographs of all alloys exhibit dendritic (D) and interdendritic (ID) regions that are typical microstructures of many HEAs. The RA01 alloy has coarse dendritic and interdendritic regions (Figure 1 a) in comparison to RA02 (Figure 1b) and RA03 (Figure 1 c) alloys.

evidence.quote: SEM images of RA03 alloy in Figure 1(c) illustrate the equiaxed shape second phase embedded in the dendritic matrix.
The higher melting temperature of Nb than other alloying elements results in the reduction of undercooling during solidiﬁcation and thus the coarser grains.

Ni partitioned to the equiaxed regions embedded in the dendritic matrix of RA03 alloy.
The elemental analysis of RA03 alloy reveals the Al pile-up at dendritic regions and minor increase in Ni and Ti at interdendritic regions.

The fracture morphology of the alloys consists of uniform dimples typical of plastic deformation. The size and the depth of the dimples are the largest for RA03 alloy in Figure 8 (c) which is consistent with its highest ductility observed during tensile loading.
The hardness values were determined as 291 ± 55 HV (2854 ± 539 MPa), 294 ± 11 HV (2833 ± 108 MPa) and 274 ± 10 HV (2687 ± 91 MPa) for as-cast RA01, RA02 and RA03 alloys, respectively.
